samples.summary: Peer-supplied `tableCellRange` row/col indices are never validated, so a remote peer's presence can drive unbounded render-path loops (tab hang) — the same DoS class the cycle guards in this delta close, through a field they do not cover
samples.evidence: Attack: any client attached to the doc (presence is writable even by a read-only viewer) publishes `activeSelection = { anchor: <any real block id>, focus: <same>, tableCellRange: { blockId: <a real table block id>, start: {rowIndex:0,colIndex:0}, end: {rowIndex:1e9,colIndex:1e9} } }`. `packages/frontend/src/app/docs/docs-view.tsx:257` copies `sel.tableCellRange` verbatim into `PeerCursor.selection` with no bounds check, and `packages/docs/src/view/editor.ts:2098` feeds it to `computeSelectionRects` on every paint (the `isRangeVisible` gate at editor.ts:2095 only looks at anchor/focus blockIds, and returns `true` for unknown ids). From there: (a) `normalizeRange` -> `normalizeCellRange` -> `expandCellRangeForMerges` (selection.ts:68-90) iterates `for (r = rowStart; r <= rowEnd; r++) for (c = colStart; c <= colEnd; c++)` over the attacker's 1e9 x 1e9 rectangle, and (b) `buildCellRangeRects` (selection.ts:685-704) runs the identical double loop. JSON presence can also carry `1e400`, which parses to `Infinity`, making `r <= rowEnd` never false — a permanently wedged tab for every other collaborator, from one presence write. Note the codebase already recognises this exact sink: `normalizeTableSpan`'s doc comment (model/numeric-attrs.ts:205-211) bands `rowSpan` precisely because `expandCellRangeForMerges` is non-terminating on unbounded values — but the *range endpoints* themselves, which reach the same loop, get no equivalent band on the peer-presence path. This code is outside the delta, but it is the remaining open door in the very threat model the delta's guards are written against.

samples.summary: No nesting-depth cap on the CRDT read path for nested tables (`treeNodeToBlock` -> `treeNodeToRow` -> `treeNodeToCell` -> `treeNodeToBlock`), nor on `computeTableLayout`/`layoutCellBlocks` — a peer-written deep nesting chain overflows the stack for every reader
samples.evidence: Vector: a peer writes a table nested inside a cell, repeated to a few tens of thousands of levels (pure CRDT node writes, no UI needed). `treeNodeToBlock` (crdt-tree.ts:213-243) recurses through rows/cells back into itself with no depth parameter, and `computeTableLayout` <-> `layoutCellBlocks` (view/table-layout.ts:133) mutually recurse once per nesting level, so `read()` or the first layout throws `RangeError: Maximum call stack size exceeded` on every reader that opens the document. The repo already treats this as a real hazard on the other two ingest paths and caps them — clipboard paste at `MAX_TABLE_DEPTH = 8` (view/clipboard.ts:71,308) and attribute banding at `MAX_BLOCK_DEPTH = 32` (model/numeric-attrs.ts:111,408, whose comment says explicitly 'a chain a peer can write to any depth — so an uncapped walk blows the stack') — but `bandBlockNumerics` only stops *descending* at 32, it does not truncate the content, so the layout recursion below it is still unbounded. I did not build a live repro, hence low confidence; the missing cap is visible in the code. Out of the delta, same untrusted-peer-data threat model.

samples.summary: `walkToTopLevelBlockId` does an O(blocks) `layout.blocks.findIndex` on every step of a peer-controlled chain, re-introducing the per-decoration linear scan the memoized `getBlockIndex` exists to avoid — cheap remote amplification of per-frame render cost
samples.evidence: The loop condition at selection.ts:133 calls `layout.blocks.findIndex(...)` once per chain step, and `normalizeRange` calls the helper twice (lines 171-178). It runs for every peer selection on every paint (view/editor.ts:2098), so cost is O(peers x chain_length x blocks) per frame, all three factors influenceable by remote peers (chain length via nesting/duplicate ids, peers via extra clients). `view/pagination.ts:345` provides exactly the memoized `getBlockIndex(layout, blockId)` for this, added per its own comment (pagination.ts:332-339) because 'each rect lookup used to findIndex over all blocks (O(blocks))' during typing. Hardening only — the cycle guard means it terminates — but the linear scan is avoidable by using the memoized lookup.

verdict.reason: Every link of the claimed chain exists in the tree. DocsPresence.activeSelection.tableCellRange (frontend/src/types/users.ts:37-41) is unvalidated peer-controlled data; yorkie-doc-store.getPresences() (line 3484-3489) returns it raw; docs-view.tsx:257 copies it verbatim into PeerCursor.selection; editor.ts:3614 stores it and repaints; editor.ts:2093-2104 passes it to computeSelectionRects on every paint, gated only by isRangeVisible (editor.ts:1998-2006) which examines anchor/focus blockIds only and returns true for unknown ids — it never inspects tableCellRange. In selection.ts, normalizeRange (142-162) -> normalizeCellRange (100-112) -> expandCellRangeForMerges (56-91) iterates `for (r=rowStart; r<=rowEnd; r++) for (c=colStart; c<=colEnd; c++)` with no clamp to table.rows.length, and buildCellRangeRects (685-704) runs the identical unclamped double loop even when the table lookup failed. Huge or Infinity endpoints therefore wedge the render loop. No clamp exists anywhere on the peer path, so neither already-guarded nor not-present applies; the repo itself bands sibling peer-written numerics (yorkie-doc-store.ts:455-461, 482-488 via normalizeTableSpan/normalizeRowHeight) for exactly this sink, which shows the range endpoints are the remaining unbanded field. Remote-controlled input driving an unbounded loop on the render path is unsafe input handling within the security lane, with availability impact on every collaborator.

verdict.reason: The claimed absence is real. `treeNodeToBlock` -> `treeNodeToRow` -> `treeNodeToCell` -> `treeNodeToBlock` (packages/docs/src/model/crdt-tree.ts:172-216) mutually recurse with no depth parameter and no cap, entered from `docsTreeToDocument` (:296-315); the frontend's duplicate reader (packages/frontend/src/app/docs/yorkie-doc-store.ts:435-536) is equally uncapped; and `layoutCellBlocks` <-> `computeTableLayout` (packages/docs/src/view/table-layout.ts:108-145, :210) mutually recurse once per nesting level with no depth argument. A repo-wide grep for depth constants finds only three caps, none of which covers this path: MAX_BLOCK_DEPTH=32 (model/numeric-attrs.ts:111) is used at :408 solely to stop the band's own walk descending and explicitly "leaves what is below as stored" (design note docs/design/docs/docs.md:290-298), so the stored nesting still reaches the uncapped layout; MAX_TABLE_DEPTH=8 (view/clipboard.ts:71, enforced :308) guards only clipboard paste; MAX_ELEMENT_DEPTH=32 (packages/backend/src/api/v1/docs-content.controller.ts:806, enforced :443/:840/:1180) guards only the REST PUT ingest, which a peer writing directly through the Yorkie CRDT bypasses. The backend's CRDT reader (packages/backend/src/yorkie/docs-tree.ts:250) delegates to the same uncapped docsTreeToDocument and contains no depth logic. Vector: a modified client writes block>row>cell>block nesting to a few thousand levels; every reader's read()/first layout throws RangeError: Maximum call stack size exceeded, making the document unopenable. This is untrusted peer-controlled input reaching an unbounded recursive parser, the same threat model the repo already hardens on its other two ingest paths.

finding.summary: Cycle guard added to three parent-chain walks, but the walks in `normalizeRange()` itself — same file, same render path, same map — are still unbounded `while` loops
finding.evidence: The change justifies its new `seen` sets with an explicit threat model: "Block ids arrive verbatim from peer-written CRDT attributes (`crdt-tree.ts`), so a parent chain that loops back on itself — a duplicated or hostile id — is representable ... an unbounded one would hang the tab" (table-layout.ts:480-486). If that model holds, it is not fully mitigated: `normalizeRange()` in the very file being edited walks the same `layout.blockParentMap` with no visited set at selection.ts:147-151 (`while (anchorTopId && layout.blocks.findIndex(...) === -1) { ... anchorTopId = parentInfo.tableBlockId; }`) and again at selection.ts:153-157 for the focus. A two-node cycle (`a -> b -> a`, neither in `layout.blocks`) never satisfies the `findIndex(...) === -1` exit and never hits a missing parent, so the loop spins forever. `normalizeRange()` runs on every render/selection read (selection.ts:566, text-editor.ts:4322), i.e. it is reached before the guarded `resolveNestedTableLayout` is. That the repo already treats cyclic parent maps as real is visible in model/range-slices.ts:74-91, which carries exactly this `seen` guard ("bounds a parent map left cyclic by a stale layout"). A guard added at three of five sibling call sites reads as covered while the reachable path stays hangable.

verdict.reason: The finding claims normalizeRange() in packages/docs/src/view/selection.ts contains two unbounded parent-chain `while` loops over layout.blockParentMap at lines 147-151 and 153-157. That is not what the file contains. Both anchor and focus walks are factored into the helper walkToTopLevelBlockId() at selection.ts:127-140, which carries exactly the `seen` cycle guard the finding says is missing: `const seen = new Set<string>([id])` (132), `if (!parentInfo || seen.has(parentInfo.tableBlockId)) break;` (135), `seen.add(id)` (137). normalizeRange calls it for the anchor at 173-176 and for the focus at 177-180. Lines 147-157 — the lines quoted as the loops — are actually the `range.tableCellRange` early-return branch and contain no loop. A whole-file sweep for `while (` returns only line 66 (expandCellRangeForMerges, a monotonic rect-expansion bounded by table dimensions, not a parent-map walk) and line 133 (the guarded walk); every other blockParentMap use (167-168, 295-296, 811-812) is a single Map.get, not a chain walk. The two-node cycle a->b->a the finding describes breaks at line 135 on the second iteration and returns an id not in layout.blocks, so findIndex === -1 at 181-183 and normalizeRange returns null — the exact behaviour requested. Render-path callers at 585 and 764 therefore cannot hang. Separately, a DoS/hang from a cyclic local layout map is at best marginal for the security lane, but the refutation does not rest on that: the guard is concretely present.

finding.summary: `resolvePositionPixel` walks the same parent map with an unguarded `while (true)` — and it is driven once per remote peer cursor per render
finding.evidence: peer-cursor.ts:121-127 is the identical walk the diff hardened elsewhere (`let currentTableId = cellInfo.tableBlockId; while (true) { const parentInfo = layout.blockParentMap.get(currentTableId); if (!parentInfo) break; nestingPath.unshift(parentInfo); currentTableId = parentInfo.tableBlockId; }`) with no `seen` set. Worse than the guarded sites, a cycle here also grows `nestingPath` without bound, so it is an unbounded allocation as well as an infinite loop — a memory-exhaustion/hang of every viewer, not only of a user who selects cells. This is the path that renders *peer* cursors, i.e. the one most directly fed by remote state, which is precisely the attacker the diff's own comment names. Not changed by this diff, but it is the sibling that makes the newly added guards incomplete.

verdict.reason: The finding claims resolvePositionPixel's parent-map walk has no `seen` set, making it an infinite loop plus unbounded `nestingPath` growth drivable by remote peer state. The working tree contradicts this: packages/docs/src/view/peer-cursor.ts:128 declares `const seenTableIds = new Set<string>([currentTableId]);`, line 132 returns `undefined` when `parentInfo.tableBlockId` was already seen (before any `unshift`), and line 135 adds each newly visited id. Since blockParentMap is finite and no id is revisited, the loop terminates and nestingPath is bounded by map size — refuting both the spin and the unbounded-allocation half of the claim. A comment at lines 122-127 explicitly names this walk as sharing `resolveNestedTableLayout`'s cycle guard and cites the peer-written-CRDT threat model. The behavior is pinned by a test: packages/docs/test/view/nested-table-cell-range.test.ts:312-323 feeds a cyclic chain (x -> a -> b -> a, built at lines 288-300) into resolvePositionPixel and asserts `undefined`; the comment at 281-287 states all three walks (resolveNestedTableLayout, normalizeRange, resolvePositionPixel) were guarded together. The reviewer's `grep 'while (true)'` would have matched line 129 — the loop is still `while (true)`, the guard is the surrounding Set, not the loop condition — which explains the missed counterexample. With no unbounded walk, there is no attacker-reachable hang or memory-exhaustion vector.
